module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 775

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/775](https://www.erdosproblems.com/775)
- [Ga25] Gao, J., *On cliques in hypergraphs*. arXiv:2510.14804 (2025).
- [MoMo65] Moon, J. W. and Moser, L., *On cliques in graphs*. Israel J. Math. (1965), 23-28.
- [Sp71] Spencer, J. H., *On cliques in graphs*. Israel J. Math. (1971), 419-421.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos775

/--
Is there a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices which contains at least $n-O(1)$ different
sizes of cliques (maximal complete subgraphs)?

The answer is no, as proved by Gao [Ga25]: more generally, for any $k\geq 3$, every $k$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains at most $n-f_k(n)$ different sizes of cliques, where
$f_k(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos775.lean"]
theorem erdos_775 : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ H : ThreeUniformHypergraph (Fin n),
      n - C ≤ (ThreeUniformHypergraph.cliqueSizes H).ncard := by
  sorry

/--
The answer is no, as proved by Gao [Ga25]: more generally, for any $k\geq 3$, every $k$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains at most $n-f_k(n)$ different sizes of cliques, where
$f_k(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_775.variants.gao :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : ThreeUniformHypergraph (Fin n),
        (ThreeUniformHypergraph.cliqueSizes H).ncard + f n ≤ n := by
  sorry

/--
For graphs, Spencer [Sp71] constructed a graph which contains cliques of at least
$n-\log_2n+O(1)$ different sizes.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_775.variants.spencer :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      (n : ℝ) - Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) - C ≤ ((SimpleGraph.cliqueSizes G).ncard : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
For graphs, Spencer [Sp71] constructed a graph which contains cliques of at least
$n-\log_2n+O(1)$ different sizes, which Moon and Moser [MoMo65] showed to be best possible.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_775.variants.moon_moser :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      ((SimpleGraph.cliqueSizes G).ncard : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) - Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) + C := by
  sorry

end Erdos775

findings.description: The docstring describes Gao’s result for every uniformity k ≥ 3, with a deficit f_k(n), but the declaration only quantifies over ThreeUniformHypergraph (Fin n). Thus it states the valid k = 3 specialization, not the general result described immediately above it. This is a documentation-scope mismatch, not an error in the specialized proposition.
findings.source_evidence: Gao, On cliques in hypergraphs, arXiv:2510.14804v3, Theorem 1.1: “For any integers k ≥ 3 and C ≥ 0, there exists a constant N=N(k,C) such that for all n ≥ N, every n-vertex k-uniform hypergraph contains no more than n-C different sizes of cliques.” Section 3 likewise states the diverging-deficit conclusion for every k ≥ 3. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14804
findings.suggested_fix: Explicitly describe this declaration as the k = 3 specialization of Gao’s theorem. Alternatively, to formalize the full result advertised by the docstring, introduce a general k-uniform hypergraph type and quantify over k ≥ 3, allowing the deficit function to depend on k.

reformulations.difference: The negative answer is expressed as False iff bounded-deficit examples exist for arbitrarily large n, rather than directly asserting Gao’s fixed-deficit upper bounds.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: False ↔ P means ¬P. Negating the existential and frequently quantifiers gives: for every C, eventually every H has fewer than n-C clique sizes. Shifting C by one makes this equivalent to Gao’s k = 3 threshold formulation: for every C, eventually every H satisfies count(H)+C ≤ n. The shift also handles the strict versus non-strict inequality; natural subtraction causes no finite-prefix loophole. This equivalence was proved without using the problem’s sorry-backed theorems in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: For the k = 3 specialization, Lean uses one natural-valued function tending to infinity, uniformly bounding all hypergraphs eventually, instead of the source’s ∀ C ∃ N threshold formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A diverging uniform deficit eventually exceeds each fixed C and therefore gives every threshold bound. Conversely, take f(n) to be the minimum of n-count(H) over all 3-uniform hypergraphs on Fin n. This collection is nonempty. The threshold bounds imply both f(n) → ∞ and, eventually, count(H)+f(n) ≤ n for every H. A generic equivalence and its specialization were proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: The asymptotic lower bound is stated with a non-strict inequality for every natural n, including zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The additive constant can absorb a strict/non-strict difference and all finitely many exceptional n. For the initial finite range, choose any graph and enlarge C until n-log₂(n)-C ≤ 0. Mathlib’s logb 2 0 = 0 is a finite boundary value and causes no obstruction. Conversely, the all-n statement immediately implies the asymptotic bound quoted in Gao’s introduction.

review.notes:
No substantive error was found in the four propositions. Both clique-size definitions count inclusion-maximal complete vertex sets, as Gao defines them. Lean proofs established finiteness of both size sets, so Set.ncard’s infinite-set default is unreachable. Executable boundary checks and proofs covered empty/small vertex types, complete graphs, a graph with maximal-clique sizes {1,2}, and a hypergraph with sizes {2,3}. Moon–Moser’s sharper bound n-floor(log₂ n), quoted by Gao, gives the stated upper bound with a bounded additive constant; n=0 is also absorbed.

The live erdosproblems.com page remained inaccessible because of Cloudflare challenges. The mathematical comparison therefore used the cited Gao paper, which explicitly records the problem, its negative solution, and both graph bounds. No status discrepancy was found in the accessible sources. The linked external proof has compatible definitions and a final statement implying the repository statement, with no sorry or custom-axiom declarations found. Its pinned Lean 4.29.1 proof could not be kernel-verified under the available Lean 4.33.1 toolchain because of compatibility errors; this is not evidence of a mathematical or status defect.
